subject: Accounting for interrupted streams — charge logic & proposal
messages:
From: Tracy Li <tracy.li@brighthealth.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aidan Chen <aidan.chen@brighthealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on streaming billing for interrupted sessions

Hi Sofia,

Quick one — we're seeing a few sessions in our integration tests where the SSE stream closes mid-response (server-side timeout), the client reconnects and requests the rest of the output, and we end up with overlapping tokens between the original partial and the resumed output. Two specific asks:

1) For hosted API usage, how does Redwood account for tokens in cases where a stream was interrupted server-side and a client reconnects to resume? Do you charge for both the partial chunk and the resumed chunk if they overlap?
2) Do you have an established credit policy when the interruption is on the Redwood side (e.g., infrastructure timeout / transient SLO miss)?

Also can you send over the baseline streaming rate card so we can model the economics if we saw ~5M streaming output tokens/month? We're preparing our internal estimate and want to understand downside risk from disconnects / retries.

Thanks — appreciate any clarity.

Tracy
Tracy Li
Director of Integrations, BrightHealth.ai
tracy.li@brighthealth.ai

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Aidan Chen <aidan.chen@brighthealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on streaming billing for interrupted sessions

Hi Tracy — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front, followed by details and next steps:

- Baseline hosted streaming price: attached (redwood_rate_card_q2_2026.pdf). For modeling, assume our public hosted streaming output rate at $0.40 / 1k output tokens (we can provide committed-discount tiers if you want a pricing model for 5M+ tokens/month).
- Token accounting behavior: by default we bill for tokens emitted by the service — if the same logical token is emitted twice (partial + resumed overlap) it will appear as two billed tokens unless the request used our recommended idempotency/session-recovery headers.
- Credit policy: we automatically issue a credit for infrastructure-initiated disconnects when the disconnect occurs within our SLO window and we can match the trace to a platform fault. We also have a customer-triggered review path if you provide traces/correlation IDs.

Next steps I suggest: please send a couple of example trace IDs and the raw client logs (session ids, timestamps). Ben (cc'd) can review the session recovery flow and confirm whether a one-off adjustment or a systemic config change (e.g., longer grace window) is preferable.

Attaching the rate card and a short diagram of our session recovery flow.

Cheers,
Sofia

Thanks Sofia — sending the traces you requested. I've attached a representative log (trace_20260418.log) and pasted the key bits below. The scenario: the Redwood stream sent ~180 tokens then closed with an HTTP/2 reset; our client reconnected and requested resume. The resumed response includes 60 tokens that overlap with the last 40 tokens of the partial.

Relevant IDs: session_id=bh-usr-77ec, trace_id=trc-20260418-993
Timestamps:
- 2026-04-18T08:23:10.512Z — SSE chunk #4 (tokens 141–180) sent, connection closed 08:23:11.041Z
- 2026-04-18T08:23:12.300Z — client reconnect + resume request
- 2026-04-18T08:23:12.658Z — server resumed and emitted tokens 171–230

So we have an overlap 171–180 that appears in both responses. Please confirm how that is billed. If you can propose how credits would be applied for the overlap in cases where Redwood-side disconnects cause the duplication, that would be ideal.

Also, we're sensitive to SLA exposure while we validate at scale — happy to consider the pilot discount you mentioned on the call if we can agree on a simple credit rule.

Best,
Tracy
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Tracy Li <tracy.li@brighthealth.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Accounting for interrupted streams — charge logic & proposal

Thanks for the traces, Tracy — that example is super helpful. Technical summary and proposed commercial handling below.

Technical behavior (how charges are computed today):
- Billing is based on tokens emitted by the model runtime and recorded in the per-session token ledger. If the same token positions are emitted twice (partial + resumed overlap) they will be two ledger entries and would be billed twice by default.
- We offer two mitigation mechanisms:
  1) Session-recovery headers (Session-ID + Resume-Offset) — when present the runtime attempts to suppress emission of already-confirmed tokens on resume. This is best-effort if the resumed model instance has access to the same KV cache.
  2) Idempotency keys for client-initiated retries — if the same request id is replayed within the dedupe window (default 30s) we suppress duplicate billing.
- Grace window: for server-side disconnects our default automated grace is 5s. If the client reconnects within 5s and the trace matches a platform-initiated close, we perform dedupe at billing reconciliation. If reconnect happens after the grace window, we typically bill both emissions.

In your example: the gap between the close (08:23:11.041Z) and the resume (08:23:12.300Z) is ~1.3s, so it falls within our 5s server-grace window. Our reconciliation should be able to identify the overlap and issue a credit for the duplicated tokens (171–180).

Commercial proposal:
- One-off operational credit: we'll credit BrightHealth.ai for the 10 duplicated tokens in the representative trace once we confirm the match in reconciliation — this will be applied as a billing adjustment on your next invoice.
- Pilot protection: for the first 90 days of your pilot we can provide a systemic protection: if more than 0.5% of streaming output tokens in a billing period are identified as duplicates from platform-initiated interruptions, we will apply a credit equal to the duplicate volume (no manual review).
- Committed discount tier: if BrightHealth.ai commits to 10M+ output tokens/month for 6 months we can offer a 20% committed usage discount on top of your tiered rate. The pilot protection and committed discount can be combined in the SOW.

Operational ask: please provide a small sample (10–20) of trace_ids across different time windows so we can validate reconciliation produces the expected dedupe. I'll coordinate with billing ops and the infra team.

I'll open a billing adjustment request once we have your sample list. Attaching a short diagram of the session recovery flow to show where the grace/dedupe happens.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Product Manager, Billing — Redwood Inference
